one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-02 to 2026-11-01. AAOI's Q3 print is estimated for Nov 5 after the close (StockAnalysis 'estimated'; prior Q3 8-K 2.02 filings came Nov 6 2025 and Nov 7 2024), so I put only ~5-10% on an in-window print or pre-announcement, in line with the supervisor's check. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 prints and 2027 capex commentary (~Oct 28-30) and peer optics prints (Celestica late Oct; Coherent/Lumentum around the turn of the month), which drive AI-optics sentiment; continuing $600M ATM supply that caps rallies; short interest 15.2% of float with only 1.6 days to cover, which can amplify moves either way. The stock bounced ~22% in four sessions off a $94 close on Sep 28, a mild argument for short-term reversal, offset by sector momentum into capex guidance. Nothing in round 2 changes this short-horizon picture (the tax add-back and multiple findings are valuation facts that matter over months, not weeks), so I keep the 1-month distribution near-neutral: lognormal centred slightly below spot (median ~$114), sigma 0.39 (139% annual vol / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend at the 2027-10-02 horizon: 0.65 x P/E ($4.21 NTM EPS x 19x = $80) + 0.35 x EV/sales ($2.9B NTM revenue x 3.5x + ~$0.2B net cash, over ~98M diluted shares = $105) = ~$89.

inputs_detail.value: Revenue $255-290M, non-GAAP GM 29-30.5%, non-GAAP net income $10.1-24.0M, EPS $0.11-0.26 on 92.8M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: ~10% below the $2.66B consensus: Q4 2026 1.6T revenue is component-constrained at $70-80M, the Pearland plant only starts production in 2027, and FY26 consensus ($1.04B) already sits below the ~$1.1B company target (Q4 needs ~$485M, +78% q/q). Capacity of ~650k units/month at YE2026 and 930k by end-2027 supports >$2B if ASPs hold.

Starts from ~0% Adjusted EBITDA in Q2 and a 4-8% net margin implied by the Q3 guide; assumes GM ~31% (vs 29.8% now; $4.60 consensus needs ~33%) and opex growing far slower than revenue. Below the ~17% the consensus implies.
Full-year 930k units/month capacity at lower ASPs; Innolight and TrendForce see 2027 demand still growing, but LightCounting's cycle history argues for slower growth by 2028, so +29% revenue growth.

84.91M outstanding Aug 20 + ~5.2M ATM shares at ~$115 + 2.9M convert + ~1.0M vested Amazon warrant (treasury) + 1.7M RSU/PSU = ~95.7M, plus room for SBC/one further small raise. Replaces my round-1 103M, which double-counted dilution already in the 92.8M guide count.

On one consistent CY2027 basis (computed from vendor FY EPS and price), the 11-peer median is 28.7x (range 10.9-47.8x) and the 6 core module/manufacturing peers' median is 21.5x. Peer multiples should compress 10-20% by Oct-2027 as next-year growth decelerates, putting a CY28-type NTM multiple for the core group near 18-19x. I use 19x, inside the range and near that core median, with no premium: AAOI's lowest GM in the core set, 99% top-10 customer concentration and negative operating cash flow are persistent negatives, while its US/Texas manufacturing is a plausible but unproven offset.

inputs_detail.derivation: Builder end of the peer range (FN 3.39x, CLS 2.88x, JBL 0.95x trailing) rather than COHR 9.5x or the Chinese pure plays (14-15x trailing on far higher margins); AAOI's ~30% GM is above the builders but its profit conversion is not yet shown. The supervisor judged 3.5x reasonable.

Jun-30 cash and restricted cash $508.8M less debt $186.4M (and $33.9M bank acceptances) = ~$0.29-0.32B; the $600M ATM roughly funds H2 capex, which exceeds H1's $625M, and 2027 capex for Pearland continues.

bear.story: Q4 guide falls well short of the ~$485M needed for ~$1.1B FY26; 1.6T ramp is component- or yield-constrained into 2027; 800G ASPs fall as Innolight/Eoptolink add capacity; margins stay near 30% GM and breakeven EBITDA; more equity. CY27 EPS ~$1.5-2 at 25-30x. AAOI's 2017-18 boom-bust (>80% drawdown) and LightCounting's 'sharp drop then recovery' cycle pattern are the base rate.

base.story: Q4/2027 come in somewhat below consensus (CY27 revenue ~$2.4B, GM ~31%, net margin ~13%); capacity reaches ~930k units/month by end-2027 with Pearland online; market pays ~22-25x on ~$4.2-4.5 NTM EPS, a little above my fair value as momentum and scarcity premium persist.

bull.story: Demand outruns supply through 2027, the Q4 step to ~$485M lands, GM moves toward 33-35%, the Amazon purchase program scales and US-made optics earn share as China-made modules face restrictions; NTM EPS ~$6.5 at ~33x, near the prior $233 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E (all on one basis, computed as price / calendar-2027 EPS from vendor fiscal-year estimates): 10.9x (Eoptolink) to 47.8x (Accelink); median of all 11 = 28.7x; median of the 6 core module/manufacturing peers (Innolight 12.2x, Eoptolink 10.9x, CLS 19.9x, FN 23.2x, COHR 28.7x, LITE 38.4x) = 21.5x. EV/EBITDA is trailing (forward not published by the source): 13.6x (JBL) to 120.3x (LITE), median 47.5x. AAOI: 25.1x CY27 consensus ($115.59 / $4.60).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19x on NTM-at-horizon (CY28-weighted) EPS: inside the range, below the 28.7x all-peer and 21.5x core CY27 medians, consistent with a 10-20% de-rating of the core median by Oct-2027 as growth slows. Note: my CY27 conversion puts Innolight and Eoptolink at 12.2x and 10.9x, lower than the vendor's 15.75x/18.65x 'Forward PE', which is a near-term blend rather than CY27 as the supervisor assumed.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. A modest discount to the core median is argued as persistent: (1) lowest gross margin in the core set (~30% vs Innolight ~46%, COHR/LITE 40-50%) with no evidence yet of improvement (Q3 guide 29-30.5%); (2) top-10 customers 99% of Q2 revenue, top-3 92%, which cannot diversify within 12 months; (3) Adjusted EBITDA ~0 and negative operating cash flow, so capacity build keeps requiring equity. The two cheapest peers (Chinese pure plays at 11-12x) carry an A-share/geopolitical discount AAOI does not, which is why I do not anchor on them, but AAOI's US-manufacturing advantage is unproven in pricing and is not used to justify a premium. Sell-side outperformance calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$60 (about 20% under the 2026 drawdown low near $76 and about half today's price) the market would be pricing a failed 1.6T ramp, loss of one of the three customers that make up 92% of revenue, or margins stuck at ~30% GM with no operating profit, rather than ordinary volatility. It equals ~13x the $4.60 CY27 consensus, ~19x my $3.18 CY27 EPS and ~2x EV/sales on CY27 revenue, levels reached only if the growth story breaks.

reasoning: Round 2 incorporates the supervisor's fact-checks, which I accept: (a) Q2's $0.06 non-GAAP EPS includes a $14.26M tax add-back and Adjusted EBITDA was -$0.54M (I re-read the 8-K exhibit), so operating leverage has not started and my 2027 margin path is now built from ~0%; (b) the verifiable CY27 consensus is $4.60 EPS / $2.66B revenue; (c) diluted shares ~98M not 103M; (d) top-10 customers 99%; (e) the KuCoin 'Serenity' post and Gaetano header are discounted and play no role. I disagree with one supervisor detail: recomputing from vendor FY estimates, Innolight and Eoptolink trade at ~12x and ~11x CY27, not 15.75x/18.65x, but the core-peer CY27 median still lands at ~21.5x, so the conclusion (AAOI at 25x CY27 is a premium it has not earned) holds. Alternative-lane evidence: the Pearland build-out (~400k sq ft, production from 2027, two independent trade/local sources) and the Sugar Land grant/hiring corroborate the physical capacity path to 930k units/month but also mean much of 2027 capacity is new-plant output with ramp risk; short interest 15% with 1.6 days to cover; no fresh Reddit/Substack signal found in October; LightCounting's cycle history argues for a sharp-drop risk once growth peaks. Valuation: P/E 19x on $4.21 NTM EPS ($80) and EV/sales 3.5x on $2.9B ($105) blend to ~$89, down from $96 (higher per-share EPS on fewer shares is more than offset by the multiple re-anchored from a mixed 36.7x median to a consistent ~21.5x core CY27 median less horizon compression). Distribution: three-lognormal mixture (bear $50 30%, base $105 46%, bull $215 24%) with median ~$103 and mean ~$123, reflecting 139% realized vol, the right skew of an AI-capacity story and the name's boom-bust history; P(>= spot) falls from 0.46 to 0.42. Research in round 2 was limited to ~7 searches/fetches; X remains unreadable.
